author: HSinghHira
description:
Ente is a self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted platform to store, share, and rediscover your photos and videos across all your devices.

**Features**

- End-to-end encryption for every photo and video you upload.

- Web app for your library plus a separate public-albums app for
  sharing.


- PostgreSQL for application data and MinIO for S3-compatible object
  storage, both bundled and pre-wired.


- Bundled Mailpit catcher for sign-up verification codes — no SMTP
  setup required to get started, with the option to switch to a real
  provider later.


- Persistent storage under /DATA/AppData/$AppID for both PostgreSQL and
  MinIO data.


**How to use?**
1. Open Ente Photos from the Zima OS dashboard.
2. Sign up for an account in the web app.
3. Open Mailpit at http://your-nas-ip:8407 and read the verification
   code.

4. Type the code into the web app to finish signing up.
5. Every new account starts with Ente's normal 10 GB limit. Raise it
   with a one-time database command — see the install tips.

6. Start uploading photos and videos, and set up a public album to
   share with others.

7. SMTP settings and the S3 address can be changed later in the
   service environment variables — no rebuild needed, just a
   container restart.

tips.before_install:
1. Find your Zima OS box's IP address. You will need it three times.
2. Open the app settings before you install.
3. In the museum service, replace CHANGEME_NAS_IP in
   ENTE_S3_B2_EU_CEN_ENDPOINT with that IP.

4. In the museum service, replace CHANGEME_NAS_IP in
   ENTE_APPS_PUBLIC_ALBUMS with that IP.

5. In the web service, replace CHANGEME_NAS_IP in ENTE_API_ORIGIN
   with that IP.

6. Do not use localhost. Phones cannot reach it.
7. Pick a new database password. Make one at randomkeygen.com.
8. Put it in ENTE_DB_PASSWORD (museum) and POSTGRES_PASSWORD
   (postgres). Both must match.

9. Pick a new storage password. Make one at randomkeygen.com.
10. Put it in ENTE_S3_B2_EU_CEN_SECRET (museum),
    MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD (minio) and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    (minio-init). All three must match.

11. Replace ENTE_KEY_ENCRYPTION, ENTE_KEY_HASH and ENTE_JWT_SECRET
    in the museum service with your own values from
    randomkeygen.com.

12. Start the Ente Photos installation.
13. Wait for the ente-minio-init container to finish before you
    sign up.

14. Open Ente Photos from the Zima OS dashboard.
15. Sign up, then read your code at http://your-nas-ip:8407.
16. Your account starts with a 10 GB limit. To raise it, run:
    docker exec ente-postgres psql -U pguser -d ente_db -c
    "UPDATE subscriptions SET storage = 109951162777600;"

17. That command sets every account on this server to about
    100 TB. Run it again any time you add a new account.

18. Important: changing a password later does not change it inside
    PostgreSQL or MinIO. Set them before the first start.

19. Important: changing ENTE_KEY_ENCRYPTION after you upload
    photos makes those photos unreadable.

title: Ente Photos (MiniO S3)
release_note:
- Switched object storage to the coollabsio community MinIO build; the official minio/minio images were pulled from Docker Hub in October 2025 and the project was archived.
- Removed the socat sidecar. It only made localhost work inside the server container, which never helped phones on the network.
- S3 endpoint, API origin and public album URL now ship as CHANGEME_NAS_IP so a wrong address fails loudly instead of half-working.
- Bucket creation moved from the discontinued minio/mc image to the AWS CLI.
- Removed the storage-unlimited container. It ran a full extra Postgres image forever just to poll one column. Raising storage is now a one-time docker exec command in the install tips.
- The Ente server and web images only publish floating tags, so there is no version field to track here.
